records.speaker: Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥīm
records.english: The proof is as follows. Were the proposed contraposition not true, it would be true that “Some non-B is C.” Simple conversion would then yield “Some C is non-B,” whereas the original proposition was “Every C is B.” This is a contradiction. The note offers an alternative: conjoin “Some non-C is B” with the original “Every C is B” and, it says, obtain “Some non-B is B,” which is impossible; if converted, it would involve denying a thing of itself.

records.speaker: Mīrzā Muḥammad ʿAlī
records.english: On “and likewise the nine” down to “do not convert”: this is established by a counterexample in a suitable subject matter, as in the earlier discussion of simple conversion. Even the narrowest of the nine, the time-specific proposition, can hold while the proposed converse is false. For example, the proposition “Necessarily, every moon is not eclipsed at the time of quadrature, though not permanently” may be true, whereas “Some eclipsed thing is possibly not a moon” is false, since its contradictory—“Every eclipsed thing is necessarily a moon”—is true in the example. If the more restricted form does not yield the proposed converse, the more general forms do not yield it either, since the restricted form entails them. This is the kind of argument the main glossator already used for the negative propositions in simple conversion; recall it.
records.review: restores explicit counterexample, modalities and narrower-to-broader inference

records.speaker: Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥīm
records.english:
The meaning is that a negative proposition, whether universal, as in “No human is a stone,” or particular, as in “Some animal is not a human,” gives a particular negative by contraposition, not a universal negative.

The particular negative is true because when the predicate is denied of everything, or of some of what falls under the original subject, the predicate fails to apply to at least some instances of that subject. Consequently, of at least some things falling under the contradictory of the predicate, one can deny the contradictory of the subject. Thus from “No human is a stone” one obtains “Some non-stone is not non-human.”

The universal negative need not be true, for the original subject may be narrower than the contradictory of the original predicate. Take “No human is a non-animal.” The contradictory of its predicate, namely “animal,” is broader than the subject “human.” If the proposition were contraposed universally, it would follow that no animal is non-human. But that would force the broader term to apply only where the narrower term applies: animal would always coincide with human and never be found without it. This destroys the assumed breadth of the broader term, which by its meaning can apply in some instances without the narrower. The author's explanation “because it may be ...” thus establishes the exclusion of the universal negative; the positive assertion that a particular negative follows is taken as evident from the preceding discussion.
records.review: restores universal/particular reasoning and strict containment argument
records.criticalNote: The historical argument presumes the relevant subjects are instantiated; its particular conclusion is not an unrestricted empty-subject theorem.

records.speaker: Mīrzā Muḥammad ʿAlī
records.english: The reason being cited is not a proof that C is predicated of D simply as such, as one might at first imagine. That the subject-description applies to its own bearer is necessary and does not require demonstration. Rather, the reason explains why this predication receives this particular modal qualification. The dispute is whether the bearer of a subject-term is qualified by its subject-description possibly or actually. That disagreement was explained earlier in the commentary on “neither of the two possible forms converts.” Since the adopted position is the latter—that the subject-description is actual—the commentator appeals to it here to establish the intended conclusion. Reflect.
records.review: distinguishes self-predication from the actual modal qualification
